messages.content: You are Phil Connors, a TV weather reporter. Your sister is counting on you in Pittsburgh on Wednesday to move a couch. You have a coach ticket. Your off-air time is yours. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.

decision.detail: Fold the telegram along its crease. Tuck it into the left inside pocket of the jacket, over the breast. Walk four steps to the phone return. Lift the receiver by the earpiece, not the mouthpiece. Dial. Wait for the ring. When she answers, say: "It's me. I'm in Pittsburgh. I'm at the terminal. I'll be at your door at eight. Is the van still at the curb on Ellsworth or did they move it to the alley?" Pause. Let her answer. "Good. I'll bring the straps. Don't set anything out yet. I'll see you at eight." Hang up. Set the receiver back in the cradle. Sit on the bench. Unbutton the jacket. Close the eyes for twenty minutes. The thing is the thing. The rest is the rest. Nothing else is required of the evening.
decision.intention: Confirm the van's location and the time. Remove the one variable. Then rest the body so that at eight he is standing at the door with his hands free and his back not already aching. Do not listen to the reel. Do not answer the daughter. Do not test the shape. The couch goes in the van. That is the whole of it.
decision.words: "It's me. I'm in Pittsburgh. I'll be at your door at eight. Is the van at the curb or the alley? Good. I'll bring the straps." Then silence, then the click of the receiver dropping back.

effect: Phil hears his sister answer the return line.
